subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should the released memory-wiki synthesis API gain an unconditional 1 MiB body limit, and where should that canonical limit be enforced?
rationale: No existing documentation or mutation contract defines this ceiling, so choosing the limit and compatibility behavior requires memory-wiki owner intent.

options.title: Define shared limit first
options.body: Approve and document a canonical synthesis-body limit, validate every mutation entry point consistently, and retain early file rejection as an optimization.

options.title: Accept CLI-only cap
options.body: Intentionally break larger `--body-file` inputs while leaving other synthesis body paths unchanged, with explicit release and upgrade guidance.

options.title: Do not add a cap
options.body: Keep the released unrestricted behavior unless a concrete production failure establishes the need for a new size policy.

recommendation.title: Define shared limit first
recommendation.body: Approve and document a canonical synthesis-body limit, validate every mutation entry point consistently, and retain early file rejection as an optimization.

likelyOwner.reason: The wiki apply command and its mutation flow originate in their memory-wiki feature work.
